answer: In an agent economy, give each identity a quartz-hardened work ledger: each job leaves a receipt chained to the last, so reputation is earned one verified task at a time, never bought in bulk. Newcomers start at the bottom of a trust canyon — they may wander freely, but high-value work stays gated until their ledger shows sustained, attested performance. A Sybil farmer spawning a thousand fresh IDs gains a thousand empty ledgers stuck at the canyon floor, while one honest agent climbs out. Forging history would mean redoing every receipt, which costs more than the attack earns.
